A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIRA study. All 25 pages, including Appendices A–K, support comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables despite layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original forecasting comparisons, missingness tests, scaling experiments and ablations in Section 4, with detailed results in Appendices J–K.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including numerical benchmark comparisons, component ablations and expert-activation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B–D retain the same CT-RoPE, frequency-specific MoE, Neural ODE extrapolation, timestamp quantization and training losses. The added citations do not change any procedure.

E1.justification: The five pretraining datasets, downstream clinical and public-health benchmarks, and evaluated missingness scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same foundation-model and full-shot baseline sets, including the medical-pretraining comparisons. None of the newly cited works is added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain the same held-out evaluation, zero-shot and full-shot settings, synthetic masking, forecast horizons, model configurations and RMSE/MAE metrics. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Sections 4.4–4.5 retain the WHO FluNet missingness tests, scaling curves, component ablations, top-k accuracy/speed comparisons and expert-activation visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Averaging results across prediction lengths remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries and graphical findings are unchanged, including the detailed results in Tables 9–13. For example, Table 5 retains MIRAbase RMSE/MAE of 0.154/0.118 and the same ablation results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, CT-RoPE derivations and Neural ODE guarantees remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is repositioned without changing its content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same methodological and benchmark contributions, 454-billion-point corpus claim, and average 10%/7% forecasting-error reduction claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of pretraining, scaling, component contributions and expert specialization are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same clinical-deployment and residual-privacy limitations.

D1.justification: Hardware, model configurations, one-epoch training, batch size, sequence length, auxiliary-loss weight, ODE tolerances and dataset access links are retained. Appendix B adds citations without adding implementation details.

R1.justification: v4 adds Term2note [9] to the introductory clinical-heterogeneity statement and two weakly supervised semantic-segmentation papers [90, 91] to Appendix B's corrective-jitter statement. All earlier references and the broader research positioning remain.

P1.justification: Citation callouts and reference numbering change, along with the arXiv version/date header. The substantive prose, terminology, headings and section order otherwise match.

P2.justification: Spacing and placement change: Table 1 moves from page 7 to 6, and Table 3 from page 9 to 8. Some numerical columns in Table 2 become crowded. Figure artwork and table contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added references modestly expand attribution, while the scientific argument and evidence remain unchanged. However, v4 crowds adjacent scores in Table 2: CDC-IHA's Neural-CDE MAE 6.766 and TimesFM RMSE 15.633 visually run together, whereas v3 separates them clearly. This introduces a limited net loss of readability.
